title: Commission 014
summary: A full concourse-level restoration emphasizing mechanical purity and patina preservation.
story: Commission 014 arrived as a forgotten relic in a dusty barn. The goal wasn't just to rebuild it, but to resurrect its soul. We preserved the exterior patina while completely re-engineering the powertrain and chassis for modern reliability without sacrificing the analog driving experience.

sections.heading: The Provenance
sections.text: Discovered in a temperature-controlled hangar in Geneva, Commission 014 arrived at our atelier as a matching-numbers rolling chassis. The vehicle had been off the road since 1989, preserved in a state of suspended animation by its second owner, a prominent Swiss horologist. Our mandate was not simply to repair, but to resurrect the machine while preserving the irreplaceable soul etched into its chassis over fifty years.

sections.heading: Mechanical Resurrection
sections.text: The beating heart of the RS, the 2.7-liter mechanically injected flat-six, required microscopic precision. The magnesium case was completely cleaned, measured, and line-bored back to zero-hour tolerances. Every fastener, bracket, and linkage was replated in period-correct yellow zinc or black oxide.

sections.heading: Tactile Authenticity
sections.text: The cabin is a study in tactile feedback and minimalist purpose. The lightweight Recaro sport seats were completely dismantled, their steel frames powder-coated, and the horsehair padding replaced with modern, durable equivalents that match original densities. Upholstered in correct grain black leatherette with Perlon corduroy inserts, the aroma inside the cabin instantly transports the driver to Stuttgart, 1973.
